answer: Time-decayed reputation capital. Each identity accrues trust only from verified past actions, with a decay curve that lets idle accounts wander toward zero. A new identity's first transactions carry a signal weight near zero, so an attacker must fund sustained genuine activity across many accounts for months before any sway. Sybil cost scales linearly with account count times the gale of ongoing upkeep—continuous real work, not a one-time fee.
